$schema_note: Context + roadmap for the Dodo desktop-pet widget. Kept in the repo so any agent has full context before touching the code. Update this whenever architecture, decisions, or roadmap change.

project.name: Dodo
project.author: Asmit Bhardwaj
project.description: A tiny pixel dog (golden retriever) that lives on the desktop and reacts to the mouse and typing.

window.positionedAt: bottom-right of the primary display work area, 24px margin
window.note: Frameless + skipTaskbar means there is NO OS close button; quitting is app-provided (see interactions.quit).

sprite.format: ASCII grid — array of fixed-width strings in renderer/dog.js (const SPRITE), each char mapped through the palette C.
sprite.rendering: drawn pixel-by-pixel on a canvas; image-rendering: pixelated; imageSmoothingEnabled=false

eyes.note: 3x3 white blocks; eyes are drawn dynamically (drawEyes) so pupils can track the cursor — those cells are skipped by drawSprite.

mouth.note: tongue anchor + tongue-pull hit region (< 6 grid cells).

sprite.constraint: All interactions are welded to these fixed anchors. Any replacement sprite must keep the same pose and eye/mouth positions, OR the anchors + drawEyes/drawTongue must be updated to match.

globalInput.loadedIn: main.js setupGlobalListeners() — wrapped in try/catch; app still runs if it fails to load, reactions just disabled.
globalInput.macosPermissions: Global hooks require macOS Input Monitoring (and often Accessibility). Cannot be granted from code. In dev (npm start) the permission attaches to the TERMINAL app; a packaged build attaches to Dodo.app. Without it the app runs but typing/cursor reactions silently do nothing.

mainToRenderer.payload: { dx, dy } — cursor offset from the dog's center

rendererToMain.handler: moves the frameless window (setPosition) for whole-body dragging
pops a native menu with Quit Dodo

ipc.preloadNamespace: window.comnyang (legacy name inherited from a cat-widget predecessor; methods: onCursorUpdate, onTypingTick, moveBy, showContextMenu)

interactions.eyeTracking: pupils shift up to 1 cell toward the cursor (drawEyes), driven by cursor-update.
interactions.blink: periodic auto-blink on a frame timer.
interactions.typingHeat: keydown raises 'heat' which tints the golden coat toward warm red; decays when typing stops.
interactions.tongue: click+drag within ~6 grid cells of the mouth stretches a springy tongue toward the pointer; releases with a spring-back.
interactions.drag: click+drag anywhere else on the body moves the whole window to any point on screen (movementX/Y deltas -> window-move-by). Cursor shows grab/grabbing.
interactions.dragHandleLegacy: a small top-center #drag-handle div using -webkit-app-region: drag still exists; now redundant with body-drag, kept for now.
interactions.quit: right-click the dog -> native context menu -> 'Quit Dodo' (app.quit()); Cmd+Q also works when focused. This is the only intended way to remove the widget.

decisions: Sprite stays as an ASCII grid in the SPRITE format (not a PNG) per user preference.
Whole-body drag implemented with physical pointer movement deltas (movementX/Y) rather than absolute coords, so it stays 1:1 and drift-free as the window slides under the cursor.
Quit exposed via right-click context menu because the window is frameless and skips the taskbar (no OS close button).
Interactions are anchor-coupled; sprite swaps must preserve eye/mouth positions.

knownIssues.summary: electron's node-based installer (extract-zip) silently produced a broken Electron.app (50KB stub binary, no Info.plist, no Electron Framework), which broke `npm start`.
knownIssues.diagnosis: The cached zip (~/Library/Caches/electron/electron-v33.4.11-darwin-arm64.zip) is valid and complete; system `unzip` extracts all 96 files. The failure is in extract-zip, not the download.
knownIssues.fix: Removed node_modules/electron/dist, re-extracted the cached zip with system `unzip` into node_modules/electron/dist, and wrote node_modules/electron/path.txt = 'Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron'. Verify with `./node_modules/.bin/electron --version` (expect v33.4.11).

knownIssues.summary: uiohook-napi global hooks need macOS Input Monitoring/Accessibility; not grantable from code.
knownIssues.status: user action required (System Settings -> Privacy & Security)

knownIssues.summary: 32x36 is very low for capturing a specific pet's likeness; a future photo->sprite feature likely needs ~48-64 grid.

roadmap.now: Perfect the current single-dog widget (polish interactions, quit, drag).
next: Refactor sprites to data files (sprites/*.json holding grid + palette + anchors) and load them dynamically — foundation for everything below.
Add a sprite picker / switcher in the app.
later: Photo -> pixel-sprite pipeline for custom pets. Recommended: TEMPLATE-BASED (fixed pose + eye/mouth regions; photo drives coat colors/markings/ear-shape) so interactions keep working. Methods considered: (a) deterministic downscale+quantize+bg-removal, (b) AI image-to-image pixel art, (c) hybrid vision-describe -> template.
Per-pet distribution: a pet is just a small data file to download; no per-pet app rebuild needed once sprites are data-driven.

howToRun.smokeTest: launch, confirm 4+ Electron processes and no errors, then quit.
